dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Priya, could we swap Thursdays for the rest of the month? I'm on lates, and Noor would otherwise be hanging about the playground on her own.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, that suits us. Freya swims at four on a Thursday, so I'm at the school gates regardless. Do you want me to run Noor straight home?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: If you would. Noor is in the later group at half four, though, so could you drop her at the pool instead?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Easy enough, the pool is on my way. They want them in the changing room ten minutes early, and those two are hopeless with their kit bags.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Then Noor will need her kit handed to her at the gate, not left in the car. It's going on the fridge calendar tonight.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm baking a two-layer chocolate sponge for my nephew's birthday on Sunday and it has to be completely dairy-free. I've got a 20cm round tin and a 23cm round tin. How much batter does each one hold?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Dairy-free is no trouble; use a hard block margarine, not a soft spread. The 20cm holds about 700ml and the 23cm about a litre, and don't fill either tin past two thirds of the way up. Can you say that back to me?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Don't fill either tin past two thirds of the way up. I'll do a double batch so I get two layers.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: A double batch gives you two even layers. Line the base with parchment and grease the sides with a little of the margarine.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Will do. I'll get the 20cm lined and greased tonight so Sunday is only mixing and baking.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Then Sunday is only the fun part. Bring the eggs out of the fridge the night before as well, because cold eggs curdle the mix.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Eggs out on Saturday night, then. The candles and the cake board are already sorted.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I fly out of Eastfield early on the ninth and want a parking space for eight days.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: There is Long Stay Blue, a ten-minute walk from departures, and Long Stay Green, with a shuttle every fifteen minutes. Both come to forty dollars for the eight days.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Forty dollars for the eight days is about what I expected. Is the booking refundable if the flight moves?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, you can cancel up to twenty-four hours ahead and get it all back.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Book me into Long Stay Green, registration KR19 TVO. I will be dropping off at six in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm cooking a mushroom stroganoff for six on Friday and one of the six doesn't eat dairy. How high should the heat be when the cream goes in?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Use an oat cream rather than soured cream so it stays dairy-free; it splits less than the soya kind. For six you want 900g of mushrooms, so three 300g punnets.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Oat cream it is, and three punnets. How high should the heat be when the cream goes in?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Get them into a wide pan in two batches as well; crowded mushrooms steam instead of browning and you lose the flavour.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Two batches in a wide pan. Everything else is already in the cupboard.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Bev, we're off to Portugal on Saturday for a week. Would Erin still be up for feeding Pickle and Nutmeg?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: She would, she has been asking all summer. College finishes at four, so it would be a teatime visit.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Teatime is perfect, they are not fussy. A pouch each in the evening, and dry biscuits left down all day. My sister Jan is popping in on the Wednesday to water the tomatoes.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Two in one week, they will be spoiled rotten. Erin is free on a Wednesday afternoon as well. Does the back door key still stick?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: A bit, you have to lift it. Then Jan can do the Wednesday feed as well, which saves a journey.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Sensible. Read the evening amount back to me and I'll put it on our calendar.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: A pouch each in the evening. Then Jan can do the Wednesday feed as well, and I'll square it with her. Everything else is written on the pad by the kettle.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I would like to switch from pay as you go to a monthly pass. Can it start on Monday the sixth rather than today?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes. The 31-day pass for zones one and two is ninety-six pounds, against a cap of a hundred and thirty-two on pay as you go.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good. It does need to start on Monday the sixth rather than today.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood, the sixth it is. Would you like a paper receipt with it as well?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: No need for that, thanks. Put it on the card I already have.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello. I've got two Ashgrove orders on the way: the oak desk on order 7731 and the desk chair on order 7802. I need to sort out the delivery days.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Of course. The oak desk is booked for Tuesday the 14th and the desk chair for Thursday the 16th. Does that fit with your week?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Not really. A neighbour can take one of them in, but for the other I must be at home, so it needs to move to a weekend. I hope there is no fee for changing a slot.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: No fee at all. We can move any delivery by up to a fortnight.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Then put the chair back to Saturday the 18th, assuming your crews work weekends.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Saturday crews run every week, so that is fine. I will send the amendment through to the depot now.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Brilliant. Send the confirmation over when it's booked.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hi, I need to send back the rain jacket from order 4482. What do I need to do at my end?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Happy to help. We take items back unworn with the tags still attached, so is that the case here?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Yes, the tags are still on it. It never left the house after it arrived, so it's exactly as it came. How long does the refund take?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Refunds land on the original card within five working days of the parcel reaching us.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That's fine by me. I'll drop the parcel off tomorrow morning.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good morning. I need to book the one-week renewal appointment at the Lancaster Road office.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can do that. The earliest is Monday the 13th at 9.15, and there is a later one on Wednesday the 15th at 2.30.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I will take the early one. Tell me what the fee covers, because I am not sure about the return postage.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: That slot is held for you. The counter opens at nine, and you will need your passport, the completed form and one photo.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: All three are in the folder already, and I do want the 9.15 rather than the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Good. Allow twenty minutes at the counter, since there is usually a short queue.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Understood, I will aim to be early. I'll bring the whole folder with me on the day.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: We are taking the ferry over to Alderwick on Saturday and want bikes for the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: There are two hire places on the island: Harbour Cycles down by the slipway, and Coast Bikes five minutes up the hill.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Either would do us. What time does the first boat leave the mainland?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: It goes from Pier Three at nine twenty, and the crossing over takes about fifty minutes.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: We will be on that one. Two bikes, please, from eleven until four.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can hold two bikes. Read the hire place and the pickup time back to me so I have it right.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Coast Bikes at eleven. We will be at the pier for nine, then.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Saturday I'm doing a paella for eight and I want it on the hob, not in the oven. How much rice should I buy?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Eighty grams a head, so 640g for eight, and about three times that in liquid. A wide pan matters more than the heat source.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That is fine, I have a 900g bag. There is a tub of chicken stock and a tub of fish stock in the freezer, and I will take the tub out tonight to thaw.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Leave it in the fridge to come round rather than on the counter, and warm it through before it meets the rice.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Overnight in the fridge, then. I've got the whole afternoon free for this.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Morning. I need to shift a booking at Fold and Fringe. Would a week's notice be enough to dodge the late-change fee?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: A week is plenty, so nothing extra to pay. There are two in your name this month: a cut and colour on Saturday the 4th, and a colour top-up on the 25th.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Right. Move the colour one over to Thursday the 16th at eleven, if there is room.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The 16th at eleven is free with Nadia, and she has the full slot. Shall I put her down for it?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Yes, go on then, that would be a weight off. Text me when it's in the diary.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Sunday I'm batch cooking two soups for the freezer, a carrot and coriander and a spiced parsnip. They both need to be thick enough to stand a spoon in. How many tubs will six litres fill?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Thick enough to stand a spoon in, noted. At 400ml a tub, six litres fills fifteen of them.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Fifteen tubs is plenty. And I do mean it about the texture, thick enough to stand a spoon in, please.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. Shall I put a shopping list together for you?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Please do, but just for one batch. I'll make the soup this weekend and leave the other until November.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: One batch it is, then. Three kilos of veg, two onions, a head of garlic and a litre and a half of stock.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Three kilos of veg, two onions, a head of garlic. The veg shop is my first stop on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello. The battery on my Pemberton cordless vacuum has stopped holding charge and I would like to claim on the warranty.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Sorry to hear that. Batteries are covered free of charge for the first twelve months, and after that there is a parts fee.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: It ran fine until a fortnight ago and now it dies after about four minutes. Does a claim need the original receipt?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: You will not need the receipt, since the order on your account covers it. I can get a collection booked from the address we hold.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That address is right. The machine is only two years old, so it is comfortably inside the twelve months.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. The driver brings a box with him, so you will not need to find packaging.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That is handy to know. Book the courier for any morning next week.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello, I'd like to get the service and MOT booked in before the end of the month.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Happy to help. I have the Skoda Octavia on your account, and its MOT runs out on the 30th, so the 22nd would suit.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The 22nd it is. Put me down for the earliest slot you have.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: That's the eight o'clock slot on the 22nd. Can you read that back so I know the line is clear?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The eight o'clock slot on the 22nd, yes.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: That matches what I have. The service and MOT together take about three hours.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: No trouble at all, I'm not in a rush. I'll drop the keys in the night before.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Colin, we're away for a fortnight from next Tuesday. Would you be able to see to our bins while we're gone, and does the food caddy go out every week or only on the recycling week?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Of course, happy to. The food caddy goes out every week; the recycling is alternate weeks only.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good to know the food caddy goes out every week. Will Ewan be back from Leeds by the second week?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: He will, so he can cover that one. Give me the weekly one again for our calendar.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The food caddy. I'll leave the side gate unlocked either way.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: We land at Terminal 2 at 7:15 on Thursday evening and need a car to the Kingsway Hotel. Four of us, three large cases, so we need the boot space.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Then I would book the XL vehicle rather than the standard saloon. That comes to around forty-six dollars all in.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Yes, book the XL vehicle rather than the standard saloon. Our travel budget caps ground transport at sixty dollars.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: XL it is. The driver will meet you in the arrivals hall at Terminal 2.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That suits us. Send the confirmation to my phone.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Afternoon. The glass carafe on my Bellweather filter machine cracked last night, and the sticker underneath says model 400.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can sort that out. The 400 takes the eight-cup carafe and the 600 takes the twelve-cup carafe, so tell me back which one I should order.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The 600 takes the twelve-cup carafe, and that is the one I need. Mine is the 600.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Added to your basket. Delivery runs two to three working days to the address we hold for you.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good. Let's get it ordered today if we can.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I want to send two gifts through Halloway's: a tea hamper going to my brother in Cardiff and a candle set going to a colleague in Leeds.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: We can do both. Gift notes are free, and ribbon wrap is £4 a parcel.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Ribbon wrap on both, then. Put a handwritten note in the Cardiff one saying 'With love from all of us'.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Noted. I will pass that wording straight to the packing team and add the ribbon wrap to both parcels.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Lovely, that all sounds right. Charge the lot to the card ending 3106.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I want to book the 09:12 to Sheffield on Tuesday. Is a seat reservation included in the advance fare?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The advance single on the 09:12 is twenty-four fifty and it gets into Sheffield at 11:40. Do you want the return leg as well?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Just the outward leg, thanks. Is a seat reservation included in the advance fare?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Outward only, then. I have you down for Tuesday morning on the 09:12.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That is right. Let's get it booked.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The wardrobe is coming Thursday between twelve and four and I am in a workshop all day. I'd rather it went straight into the spare room than the hall. Could you be in for it?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can work at the kitchen table that day, so yes. The boxes can go straight into the spare room. Dan next door still has our drill.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'd rather it went straight into the spare room than the hall. Theo gets in on Friday evening and we are building it on the Saturday morning, so the room will be ready for him.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Fair enough. I'll shift the recycling out of there on Wednesday night, then.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good thinking. The Allen keys are in the kitchen drawer.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm scaling up the lemon drizzle traybake for twelve tomorrow and it's written for eight. Can I use golden caster sugar instead of white for the drizzle?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Golden caster is fine there; it only deepens the colour a shade. For twelve, go up by half: 300g flour, 300g sugar, 300g butter and six eggs.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good. I've got 200g of butter in the fridge, which is plenty, so I won't need to shop. How long does it want in the oven?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Fifty minutes at 170C fan, and slide a skewer into the middle at forty-five to check.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'll test it with a skewer, then. I'll set everything out on the counter tonight.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Dev, the fibre engineer is coming Thursday between eight and twelve and I'm at the depot all day. Do they want the old router handed back on the day?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Lectures till eleven for me, I'm afraid. Maureen is about in the morning though, she's here for the extractor fan.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That helps. He'll want the cupboard under the stairs and nothing else, so he will not be long.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I'll chalk a mark on the cupboard door for him. Aisha is off nights, so she'll be asleep upstairs.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Then Maureen can let him in and keep him downstairs.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I'll leave Maureen a note by the kettle. Say the day back to me and I'll put it in my phone.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Thursday. Right, I'd better get back to the depot.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I've got two joints in the fridge for tomorrow, a 1.6kg lamb shoulder and a 2kg pork loin. How long does each want in the oven?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The lamb wants ninety minutes at 160C fan, then fifteen minutes under foil; the pork wants an hour and three quarters at 180C. Can you read the lamb timing back to me?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Ninety minutes at 160C fan, then fifteen minutes under foil. I'll put the lamb in at five and take it out at six.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: That is it exactly. Bring the lamb out of the fridge an hour before it goes in, or the middle stays cold.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Out of the fridge at four, then. I'll jot the timings on the board by the hob.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hello. I left a navy suit jacket and a wool coat with you last week, and I need to come in for a fitting.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Of course, both are on the rail. Elif has Friday at half four, or Saturday at eleven if the weekend is easier.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Saturday would be easier, actually. What would you charge to shorten the coat sleeves?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Saturday at eleven, then. Elif will have both pieces pressed and hanging ready for you.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That works nicely for me. I'll come straight from the office.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The mixer tap in our kitchen has started dripping properly overnight. When can you get someone out?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can send Ray on Thursday the fifteenth. He'll need the water off at the mains, and in your building the stopcock sits inside the upstairs flat. Can you confirm the flat number for me?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Flat 3B. So he'll need the water off at the mains, and Graham upstairs is away until the twelfth, with Tom letting Ray in downstairs.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Got it, 3B. I'll put Ray down for nine o'clock and email the job number over this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That's great, thanks. There's a bucket under it in the meantime.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hi. I have two Cobblestone subscriptions running on the same account: the fortnightly house blend and the monthly decaf.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: I can see both of them. The house blend renews on the 4th and the decaf renews on the 20th.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I do not want any more bags stacking up in the cupboard, I have three unopened already. Put the decaf on hold until September.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Understood. I will set the hold to begin at the end of July so nothing goes out next month.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I do not want any more bags stacking up in the cupboard. Leave everything else on the account exactly as it is.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Hi, I'd like to book a cleaning at the Riverside dental clinic. Also, do you know whether they validate parking for patients?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, they validate parking for patients. I have Thursday at 2pm or Friday at 10am available.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Thursday at 2pm is better for me, and it's good that they validate parking for patients.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Thursday at 2pm. Could you read back the day and time so I can confirm?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Thursday at 2pm. Can we go ahead and lock that in?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. I'd like a slot at the Year 4 parents' evening for Rosa. What hours is Mrs Adeyemi seeing parents?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: She is seeing parents from four until six on Thursday the 9th, and there are gaps left at 4.40 and at 5.20.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: We will take 5.20. Neither of us can get away from work before half past four, so that is comfortable.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Noted, 5.20 on the Thursday with Mrs Adeyemi. Will you be bringing Rosa along on the night?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Yes, she will come along too. I appreciate you fitting us in.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: I'm getting the train to Ashfield on Saturday and then on to the Greenbank centre. I'll have a large case with me.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Two buses will get you there. The 184 runs from Ashfield station to the Greenbank centre every twenty minutes, and the 187 does the same trip hourly but stops nearer the entrance.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: Before I commit, is there a lift down to the bus stands?

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: Yes, a lift runs from the concourse straight down to the stands, and both buses are low-floor.

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: That settles it, then. I'll be travelling first thing on Saturday morning.

dialogue.speaker: assistant
dialogue.text: The first services go at six on Saturdays. Could you just confirm the bus number and the starting point for me?

dialogue.speaker: user
dialogue.text: The bus runs from Ashfield station to the Greenbank centre. I'll text you when I set off.
